newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases, differentials stable.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases, differentials stable.

text.p: Gas oil outright prices eased on Friday with a slide in near-month futures while differentials were stable in very quiet discussion, traders said.
July IPE last traded down $2.50 a tonne at $162, while August IPE ended $2 lower at $163.75 in a follow-through to Thursday's Brent-inspired losses.

Physical trade was slowed by the U.S. Independence Day holiday. The only cargo trade heard was low sulphur diesel for delivery in the second half of July at August IPE +$3.75 cif Le Havre, little changed from Thursday's level of July IPE +$4.50.
The purchaser of Friday's cargo is a low sulphur diesel producer, showing that supply is fairly tight and also that some refiners are switching to production of heating oil.
"There isn't that much around. People are looking to pick off cargoes to put into storage," a trader said, adding there was also a scarcity of Russian and Algerian.
Earlier a low sulphur diesel cargo was offered firmly at August +$5.50 and bid at +$4. A cargo of Russian low sulphur diesel was bid at July +$1/2 for a voyage to Amsterdam.
Barges were dormant. As the screen fell heating oil offers crept upwards to 75 cents over July IPE from 50 cents.
